paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תֹּלְד֥וֹת עֵשָׂ֖ו ה֥וּא אֱדֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And these are the generations of Esav (the same is Edom).

paragraphs.commentary:
**The verse opens the Esav-toledot block with the first of four *hu Edom* / *avi Edom* identification-refrains that bracket the chapter (vv 1, 8, 19, 43; with a v 9 variant *avi Edom*).** The refrain is editorially-load-bearing — it asserts the Esav=Edom equation four times in 43 verses — and is structurally distinct from the Gen 25:25/30 birth-and-stew etymology (covered by the central-glossary `esau-edom-name-etymology-double-play` entry). The fourfold-refrain is a chapter-36-specific structural device housed in the per-translation overlay (see `hu-edom-fourfold-refrain-toledot-structure`).

Modern critical scholarship (**Skinner** *ICC Genesis* 1910 pp. 430-434; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 559-563; **Hamilton** *NICOT Genesis 18-50* 1995 pp. 388-405; **Friedman** *The Bible with Sources Revealed* 2003) treats the refrain as a P-source redactional bracketing-device that unifies a chapter compiled from at least two distinct genealogical sources (the *bnei Esav* + *alufei bnei Esav* material at vv 9-19 and the *bnei Se'ir ha-Chori* material at vv 20-30). The Horite-section (vv 20-30) and the king-list (vv 31-39) are *not* closed with the Edom-refrain — only the Esav-blocks are, which confirms the structural-function of the refrain as marking the close of Esav-units within the chapter.

The cross-corpus Esav=Edom equation that the refrain asserts is foundational for the entire HB Edom-tradition: Num 20:14-21, Deut 2:4-8, Deut 23:8 [MT 23:9], Obadiah, Mal 1:2-5, Ps 137:7, Lam 4:21-22, Ezek 25:12-14 + 35:1-15, Joel 4:19 [MT 4:19]. The verse's structural-load is therefore not only chapter-internal but corpus-wide.

paragraphs.text: עֵשָׂ֛ו לָקַ֥ח אֶת־נָשָׁ֖יו מִבְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן אֶת־עָדָ֗ה בַּת־אֵילוֹן֙ הַֽחִתִּ֔י וְאֶת־אָהֳלִֽיבָמָה֙ בַּת־עֲנָ֔ה בַּת־צִבְע֖וֹן הַֽחִוִּֽי׃

i18n.en: Esav took his wives from the daughters of Kena'an: Adah the daughter of Elon the Chitti, and Oholivamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tziv'on the Chivvi,

paragraphs.commentary:
**Gen 36:2-3 is the third of three HB attestations of Esav's wife-list (Gen 26:34 + Gen 28:9 + Gen 36:2-3), and the three lists do not match cleanly.** The chapter-26 entry (`morat-ruach-bitterness-of-spirit-esau-hittite-wives`) covers the chapter-26 narrative-setup function (the wives' effect on Yitzchaq and Rivkah, the Gen 27:46 dialogue-quotation back-link); the Gen 36-side specifically introduces material — particularly the integration of Oholivamah into the Anah-Tziv'on Horite-Se'irite lineage — that does not appear there. The Gen 36-side is housed in a sibling overlay entry (`esav-wives-list-three-chapter-doublet-gen-36-side`) per the ratified sibling-overlay-entries pattern.

**The discrepancies.** *Basemat bat-Elon ha-Chitti* of Gen 26:34 corresponds to *Adah bat-Elon ha-Chitti* of Gen 36:2 (same patronymic, different given-name); *Machalat bat-Yishma'el achot Nevayot* of Gen 28:9 corresponds to *Basemat bat-Yishma'el achot Nevayot* of Gen 36:3 (same patronymic and clan-relation, different given-name); *Yehudit bat-Be'eri ha-Chitti* of Gen 26:34 has no clean counterpart at Gen 36:2-3, with the possible counterpart being *Oholivamah bat-Anah bat-Tziv'on ha-Chivvi* (different patronymic, different ethnonym). The harmonizing-rabbinic reading (**Gen Rab 65:2**; **Rashi** at Gen 36:2) treats the differently-named wives as the same persons under multiple names. The source-critical reading (**Wellhausen** *Prolegomena* 1885; **Skinner** *ICC Genesis* 1910 pp. 425-426; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 427-428, 558-560; **Friedman** *Who Wrote the Bible?* 1987 + *The Bible with Sources Revealed* 2003; **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 202, 280-281; **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 186-187, 248) treats the three lists as drawn from distinct source-strata (J or J-supplement for Gen 26; redactional bridge for Gen 28:9; P or late-P for Gen 36), preserved without smoothing-to-harmony.

**The Chivvi-vs-Chori variant.** The MT at v 2 names Anah's grandfather Tziv'on as *ha-Chivvi* (Hivite), but at v 20 the same Tziv'on appears as a son of Se'ir *ha-Chori* (the Horite). The Samaritan Pentateuch and the LXX at Gen 36:2 read *ha-Chori* (correcting to match v 20). Modern critical scholarship (**BHS** apparatus; **Westermann** p. 561; **Speiser** pp. 280-281; **Hamilton** pp. 393-394; **Skinner** *ICC* p. 432) generally treats the MT *ha-Chivvi* as a scribal-error or tradition-variant for *ha-Chori*. The Hivite-vs-Horite confusion here is independent of the broader Hivite-vs-Hittite confusion in Genesis (Gen 34:2 Chivvi Shechem; covered separately) and is a chapter-36-specific text-critical question. The translation preserves the MT *Chivvi* per the standing principle of translating the principal reading; the Chori-variant is documented in `chorim-horites-hurrian-or-cave-dweller-identification`.

paragraphs.commentary: **The MT preserves a ketiv/qere at the first-son's name: ketiv יעיש (Ye'ish) / qere יְעוּשׁ (Ye'ush).** The qere *Ye'ush* is the form transmitted at the parallel 1 Chr 1:35 and is adopted by ASV / KJV / NJPS / NRSV. The Wheel of Heaven Translator Brief's standing principle is to translate the qere; the ketiv is preserved in the underlying source-text field. The ketiv-qere question may reflect either an older orthographic form, a scribal-variant, or a metathesis (a swap of *yod* and *vav* in the medial position). The same ketiv/qere recurs at vv 14 and 18.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־הָיָ֧ה רְכוּשָׁ֛ם רָ֖ב מִשֶּׁ֣בֶת יַחְדָּ֑ו וְלֹ֨א יָֽכְלָ֜ה אֶ֤רֶץ מְגֽוּרֵיהֶם֙ לָשֵׂ֣את אֹתָ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י מִקְנֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together; and the land of their sojournings could not bear them because of their cattle.

paragraphs.commentary: **The verse's *rekhusham rav mi-shevet yachdav* (*their substance was too great for them to dwell together*) is structurally a deliberate echo of the Gen 13:6 Avraham-Lot separation: *v-lo nasa otam ha-aretz lashevet yachdav ki-hayah rekhusham rav v-lo yakhlu lashevet yachdav* — *and the land was not able to bear them, that they might dwell together; for their substance was great, so that they could not dwell together*.** The vocabulary is essentially identical (*rekhush rav*, *shevet yachdav*, *nasa*-or-*yakhlah ha-aretz*). The editorial-echo positions the Esav-Ya'aqov separation as a structural-rhyme of the Avraham-Lot separation: in both cases, the patriarch's-line stays in the land while the collateral-line departs to a separate territory (Lot to Sodom-Plain → Mo'av/Ammon eventually; Esav to Se'ir → Edom). Modern critical scholarship (**Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* p. 560; **Hamilton** *NICOT* p. 391) reads the echo as a P-redactional patterning.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב עֵשָׂו֙ בְּהַ֣ר שֵׂעִ֔יר עֵשָׂ֖ו ה֥וּא אֱדֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And Esav dwelt in Mount Se'ir: Esav is Edom.

paragraphs.commentary: **The second of the chapter's four *hu Edom* refrains.** Here the formula adds the geographical Se'ir-locus to the equation: *Esav b-har Se'ir* + *Esav hu Edom* together stage the triple-identification Esav = Se'ir-dweller = Edom. The Se'ir-Edom geographical equation is HB-pervasive (Gen 32:4; 33:14, 16; 36:9, 20-30; Deut 2:4-5, 2:12, 22; cf. the central-glossary `esau-edom-name-etymology-double-play` entry on the *sear* → *Seir* paronomastic foreshadow at Gen 25:25). The chapter's structural-section closes at v 8: the v 1-8 block (introduction + relocation) terminates with the *Esav hu Edom* identification-refrain (see the central overlay entry `hu-edom-fourfold-refrain-toledot-structure`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה תֹּלְד֥וֹת עֵשָׂ֖ו אֲבִ֣י אֱד֑וֹם בְּהַ֖ר שֵׂעִֽיר׃

i18n.en: And these are the generations of Esav, the father of Edom in Mount Se'ir.

paragraphs.commentary: **The second toledot-formula in the chapter opens the Esav-genealogy proper.** The chapter's two toledot-formulae (v 1 and v 9) is editorially significant: modern critical scholarship (**Skinner** *ICC* pp. 430-434; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* p. 561; **Friedman** *The Bible with Sources Revealed* 2003) reads the doubling as evidence that the chapter is compiled from at least two distinct genealogical sources, with v 1 opening the introductory section (vv 1-8) and v 9 opening the genealogy-proper (vv 9-19). The v 9 formula uses the variant *avi Edom* (father of Edom) in place of the *hu Edom* (the same is Edom) of vv 1, 8, 19 — the variant is the second member of the chapter's fourfold-refrain-set, with the closing v 43 using the fullest form *hu Esav avi Edom*.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֖לֶּה שְׁמ֣וֹת בְּנֵֽי־עֵשָׂ֑ו אֱלִיפַ֗ז בֶּן־עָדָה֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֔ו רְעוּאֵ֕ל בֶּן־בָּשְׂמַ֖ת אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: These are the names of Esav's sons: Elifaz the son of Adah the wife of Esav; Re'u'el the son of Basemat the wife of Esav.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְי֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י אֱלִיפָ֑ז תֵּימָ֣ן אוֹמָ֔ר צְפ֥וֹ וְגַעְתָּ֖ם וּקְנַֽז׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Elifaz were Teman, Omar, Tzefo, and Ga'tam, and Qenaz.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Teman, named here as the firstborn-son of Elifaz son of Esav, is the structural-eponym of the Edomite clan and territory of Teman.** The Teman-locus is associated in the HB with wisdom-traditions: **Jer 49:7** asks *im od chokhmah b-Teman* — *is there no longer wisdom in Teman?*; **Obad 8-9** pairs the *chakhamim me-Edom* (wise-men from Edom) with the *gibborim Teman* (mighty-men of Teman) in the judgment-oracle. The Job-corpus's *Elifaz the Temanite* (Job 2:11; אֱלִיפַז הַתֵּימָנִי) shares the name *Elifaz* and the locus *Teman* with the Gen 36:11 figure.

The traditional rabbinic reading (**b. Bava Batra 15b**; **Genesis Rabbah 76:1**) and some modern conservative scholarship (**Hamilton** *NICOT* p. 392; **Wilson** *Job* NICOT 1988) identify Job's Eliphaz the Temanite as the same figure or as descended from the Gen 36 Elifaz-Teman line. Modern critical scholarship (**Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* p. 562; **Pope** *Job* AB 1973; **Clines** *Job* WBC 1989-2011; **Newsom** *The Book of Job* 2003) reads the Temanite-locale connection as the only certain link and treats the personal-name identity as either coincidental or as the wisdom-tradition's deliberate evocation of the Edom-as-wisdom-locus motif. The Job-link is flagged here without resolution; the cross-corpus question is deferred to a future Job-translation pipeline.

paragraphs.text: וְתִמְנַ֣ע ׀ הָיְתָ֣ה פִילֶ֗גֶשׁ לֶֽאֱלִיפַז֙ בֶּן־עֵשָׂ֔ו וַתֵּ֥לֶד לֶאֱלִיפַ֖ז אֶת־עֲמָלֵ֑ק אֵ֕לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י עָדָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: And Timna was concubine to Elifaz the son of Esav; and she bore to Elifaz Amaleq. These are the sons of Adah the wife of Esav.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Gen 36:12 is structurally the seed-verse of the Amaleq-as-archetypal-enemy-of-Israel tradition.** Timna, named here as Elifaz's concubine (*pilegesh*), bears Amaleq to Elifaz — making Amaleq the grandson of Esav and a great-great-grandson of Avraham through the collateral-line. The genealogical-placement is editorially-load-bearing: the archetypal enemy of Israel is, by descent, Israel's near-kin.

**The cross-corpus Amaleq-tradition.** **Exod 17:8-16** (the Refidim battle; the *milchamah la-YHWH ba-Amaleq mi-dor dor* divine-oath; *macho emcheh et-zekher Amaleq*); **Num 24:20** (Bil'am's oracle: *reshit goyim Amaleq*); **Deut 25:17-19** (the *zakhor et asher asah lekha Amaleq* command); **1 Sam 15** (Sha'ul's failed *cherem* on Agag); **1 Sam 30** (David at Tziqlag); **2 Sam 1:1-16** (the Amaleqite executed by David); **Est 3:1** (Haman *ha-Agagi* as the Amaleqite-archetype-revenant). The Sha'ul-Mordokhai-Esther / Agag-Haman / Yisra'el-Amaleq triple-parallel runs through the canonical-redaction.

**The Timna-double-identification.** Gen 36:22 names *achot Lotan Timna* (Lotan's sister Timna) among the Horite sons of Lotan. Modern critical scholarship (**Sarna** *JPS* p. 250; **Westermann** p. 562; **Wenham** p. 338) treats this Timna as the same figure as the v 12 concubine of Elifaz. The double-identification places Amaleq's mother as a Horite — meaning Amaleq is matrilineally Horite and patrilineally Esavite, structurally embedded at the seam between the displacing-Esavite and the displaced-Horite populations.

**The 1 Chr 1:36 variant.** The Chronicler's parallel lists Amaleq differently — as a direct son of Elifaz alongside Teman, Omar, Tzefi, Ga'tam, Qenaz, and Timna — omitting the concubine-detail. Modern critical scholarship (**Klein** *1 Chronicles* Hermeneia 2006; **Knoppers** *1 Chronicles 1-9* AB 2003) reads the Gen 36:12 concubine-detail as editorially-deliberate, downgrading the Amaleq-line within the Esavite hierarchy.

See the central-glossary `amaleq-timna-genealogy-archetypal-enemy-origin` for the full cross-corpus apparatus. The lens-discipline pattern applies: any WoH-distinctive reading of the Amaleq-archetype is wiki-reserved.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י רְעוּאֵ֔ל נַ֥חַת וָזֶ֖רַח שַׁמָּ֣ה וּמִזָּ֑ה אֵ֣לֶּ֣ה הָי֔וּ בְּנֵ֥י בָשְׂמַ֖ת אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Re'u'el: Nachat, and Zerach, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemat, Esav's wife.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֣לֶּה הָי֗וּ בְּנֵ֨י אָהֳלִיבָמָ֧ה בַת־עֲנָ֛ה בַּת־צִבְע֖וֹן אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֑ו וַתֵּ֣לֶד לְעֵשָׂ֔ו אֶת־יעיש [יְע֥וּשׁ] וְאֶת־יַעְלָ֖ם וְאֶת־קֹֽרַח׃

i18n.en: And these were the sons of Oholivamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Tziv'on, Esav's wife: and she bore to Esav Ye'ush, and Ya'lam, and Qorach.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֖לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־עֵשָׂ֑ו בְּנֵ֤י אֱלִיפַז֙ בְּכ֣וֹר עֵשָׂ֔ו אַלּ֤וּף תֵּימָן֙ אַלּ֣וּף אוֹמָ֔ר אַלּ֥וּף צְפ֖וֹ אַלּ֥וּף קְנַֽז׃

i18n.en: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esav: the sons of Elifaz the firstborn of Esav: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Tzefo, chief Qenaz,

paragraphs.commentary:
**The lexeme *aluf* (אַלּוּף — clan-chief) is editorially-load-bearing in this chapter — it appears approximately forty times across vv 15-43 as the technical title of an Edomite or Horite clan-head.** Outside Gen 36 / 1 Chr 1, the clan-chief sense is distributed at **Exod 15:15** (*alufei Edom*, in the Song of the Sea — one of the earliest Hebrew compositions per Cross & Freedman 1975); **Jer 13:21**; **Zech 9:7, 12:5-6**. The lexeme's tribal-confederation pre-statehood register is editorially-distinctive of the Edomite/Horite material.

**The chapter's *alufim* → *melakhim* → *alufim* diachronic compression.** The chapter stages the *alufim* (vv 15-19, 21, 29-30) → *melakhim* (vv 31-39) → *alufim* (vv 40-43) sequence. **Bartlett** *Edom and the Edomites* JSOTSup 77 (1989) pp. 86-102 reads the pattern as preserving a real Iron-Age Edomite political-history (clans → kings → clans). The non-dynastic-succession formula of the king-list (each king from a different city, no son-of-his-predecessor formula) is consistent with a tribal-confederation pre-statehood organization.

**Translation choice.** The WoH preserves ASV-baseline *chief* throughout. The KJV *duke* is anachronistic (medieval-European-feudal connotations); NJPS / NRSV *clan* loses the singular-leader register. See the central-glossary `aluf-edomite-clan-chief-tribal-confederation` entry.

paragraphs.text: אַלּֽוּף־קֹ֛רַח אַלּ֥וּף גַּעְתָּ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף עֲמָלֵ֑ק אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֤י אֱלִיפַז֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֔וֹם אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י עָדָֽה׃

i18n.en: chief Qorach, chief Ga'tam, chief Amaleq. These are the chiefs that came of Elifaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י רְעוּאֵל֙ בֶּן־עֵשָׂ֔ו אַלּ֥וּף נַ֙חַת֙ אַלּ֣וּף זֶ֔רַח אַלּ֥וּף שַׁמָּ֖ה אַלּ֣וּף מִזָּ֑ה אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֤י רְעוּאֵל֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֔וֹם אֵ֕לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י בָשְׂמַ֖ת אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Re'u'el, Esav's son: chief Nachat, chief Zerach, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs that came of Re'u'el in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemat, Esav's wife.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֗לֶּה בְּנֵ֤י אָהֳלִֽיבָמָה֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת עֵשָׂ֔ו אַלּ֥וּף יְע֛וּשׁ אַלּ֥וּף יַעְלָ֖ם אַלּ֣וּף קֹ֑רַח אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֞י אָֽהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה בַּת־עֲנָ֖ה אֵ֥שֶׁת עֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Oholivamah, Esav's wife: chief Ye'ush, chief Ya'lam, chief Qorach. These are the chiefs that came of Oholivamah the daughter of Anah, Esav's wife.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֧לֶּה בְנֵי־עֵשָׂ֛ו וְאֵ֥לֶּה אַלּוּפֵיהֶ֖ם ה֥וּא אֱדֽוֹם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: These are the sons of Esav, and these are their chiefs: the same is Edom.

paragraphs.commentary: **The third *hu Edom* refrain closes the first *alufim*-list (vv 15-19) and the broader Esav-genealogy-proper block (vv 9-19).** The MT marks the close with a *setumah* (ס) paragraph-marker, confirming the editorial-structural division between the Esav-block and the following Horite-block (vv 20-30). The Horite-block, structurally-separate from the Esav-blocks, is *not* closed with the Edom-refrain — only the Esav-blocks are.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֤לֶּה בְנֵֽי־שֵׂעִיר֙ הַחֹרִ֔י יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָ֑רֶץ לוֹטָ֥ן וְשׁוֹבָ֖ל וְצִבְע֥וֹן וַעֲנָֽה׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Se'ir the Chori, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, and Shoval, and Tziv'on, and Anah,

paragraphs.commentary:
**The Horite genealogy opens here (vv 20-30), structurally-separate from the Esav-genealogy (vv 9-19) and bracketed at v 30 with a closing-formula but without the *hu Edom* refrain (the refrain marks only Esav-blocks; the Horite-block is a parallel autochthonous-population register, not an Esavite sub-unit).** The phrase *yoshvei ha-aretz* (*the inhabitants of the land*) is editorially-significant: it names the Horites as the *autochthonous* pre-Edomite population of Se'ir, consistent with the Deut 2:12 / Deut 2:22 framing (*u-v-Se'ir yashvu ha-Chorim l-fanim u-vnei Esav yirashum* — *and in Se'ir the Chorim dwelt formerly, and the children of Esav displaced them*).

**The Horite-identification crux.** The HB *Chorim* are a philologically-contested ethnonym. **Reading (a)**: Hurrian-identification (**Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 pp. 282-283; *Hurrians and Subarians* JAOS Supplement 13 (1948); **Albright** *BASOR* 163 (1961); **Wilhelm** *The Hurrians* 1989; **De Vaux** 1978) — the HB *Chorim* are remnants of the Mitanni-era Hurrian diffusion into the southern Levant. **Reading (b)**: cave-dweller folk-etymology (**Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 564; **Hamilton** *NICOT* pp. 395-396; **Bartlett** *Edom and the Edomites* 1989 pp. 78-81) — the ethnonym derives from Hebrew *chor* (*hole, cave*) in a folk-etymological *cave-dweller / troglodyte* sense; the onomastic-evidence of the Gen 36 list does not support the Hurrian-identification. The crux is genuinely unresolved; see the central-glossary `chorim-horites-hurrian-or-cave-dweller-identification` entry for the full apparatus.

**Normalization note.** The chapter-14 stable text reads *the Horites* (ASV-baseline transliteration) at GEN-WOH-14:6; the chapter-36 draft reads *Chori* / *Chorim* (WoH-transliterated). The chapter-36 transliteration is preferred for cross-corpus consistency with other proper-noun transliterations; chapter-14 is flagged for retroactive update under a corpus-normalization pass.

paragraphs.text: וְדִשׁ֥וֹן וְאֵ֖צֶר וְדִישָׁ֑ן אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י בְּנֵ֥י שֵׂעִ֖יר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: and Dishon, and Etzer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs that came of the Chorim, the sons of Se'ir in the land of Edom.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵי־לוֹטָ֖ן חֹרִ֣י וְהֵימָ֑ם וַאֲח֥וֹת לוֹטָ֖ן תִּמְנָֽע׃

i18n.en: And the sons of Lotan were Chori and Hemam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.

paragraphs.commentary: **Timna, named here as Lotan's sister within the Horite genealogy, is per the dominant modern critical reading (Sarna, Westermann, Wenham) the same figure as the v 12 concubine of Elifaz son of Esav.** The double-identification places Amaleq's mother as a Horite — meaning Amaleq is matrilineally Horite and patrilineally Esavite, structurally-embedded at the seam between the two populations the chapter is documenting. See the central-glossary `amaleq-timna-genealogy-archetypal-enemy-origin` entry for the full discussion of the Timna-double-identification and its consequences for the Amaleq-archetype tradition.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י שׁוֹבָ֔ל עַלְוָ֥ן וּמָנַ֖חַת וְעֵיבָ֑ל שְׁפ֖וֹ וְאוֹנָֽם׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Shoval: Alvan, and Manachat, and Eival, Shefo, and Onam.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֥לֶּה בְנֵֽי־צִבְע֖וֹן וְאַיָּ֣ה וַעֲנָ֑ה ה֣וּא עֲנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָצָ֤א אֶת־הַיֵּמִם֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בִּרְעֹת֥וֹ אֶת־הַחֲמֹרִ֖ים לְצִבְע֥וֹן אָבִֽיו׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Tziv'on: Ayyah, and Anah; this is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Tziv'on his father.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The lexeme *yemim* (הַיֵּמִם) is a Hebrew Bible hapax legomenon and is one of the most-contested philological cruxes in the patriarchal narratives. The crux is genuinely philologically-unresolved; at least five distinct readings are attested.**

**(a) Hot springs / thermal waters** (dominant modern-majority): LXX (with manuscript variation), Vulgate *aquas calidas*, Jerome, Symmachus *thermae*; **Sarna** *JPS* pp. 251-252; **Westermann** pp. 565-566; **Speiser** p. 283; **Hamilton** p. 398; **Wenham** p. 339; **Alter** p. 204; ASV / NJPS / NRSV / NIV / ESV. The reading is geographically-supported (the Edomite-territory thermal-spring tradition) and is the WoH-baseline translation.

**(b) Mules** (pre-modern Western majority): **b. Pesachim 54a** identifies *yemim* with mules and reads Anah as the inventor of cross-breeding horses and donkeys (a Deut 22:9-11 *kil'ayim* transgression). **Rashi** at Gen 36:24 reproduces the Talmudic reading; KJV *mules* follows the Vulgate's pre-Jerome tradition.

**(c) Demons / spirits**: **Targum Pseudo-Jonathan**; **Genesis Rabbah 82:14** minority.

**(d) Onqelos *eimanaya*** (variously *the giants*, *the warm waters*, *the strong-ones*, or *the Emim-people*; genuinely ambiguous in Aramaic).

**(e) Emendation to *eimim*** — the Rephaim-cluster autochthonous-giants of Deut 2:10-11, 2:20. **Skinner** *ICC* p. 433 considers but does not adopt; rejected by Speiser, Westermann, Sarna, Hamilton, Alter, Wenham (paleographically not clean — yod-aleph confusion).

**Translation choice.** The WoH preserves ASV-baseline *hot springs* per the modern-majority reading and the standing principle of accuracy-above-lens. The five-reading apparatus is documented in the central-glossary `yemim-hapax-hot-springs-mules-demons-lens-discipline` entry; lens-discipline applies (no WoH-distinctive synthesis). Any WoH-distinctive reading of *yemim* is wiki-reserved.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֥לֶּה בְנֵֽי־עֲנָ֖ה דִּשֹׁ֑ן וְאָהֳלִיבָמָ֖ה בַּת־עֲנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Anah: Dishon, and Oholivamah the daughter of Anah.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י דִישָׁ֑ן חֶמְדָּ֥ן וְאֶשְׁבָּ֖ן וְיִתְרָ֥ן וּכְרָֽן׃

i18n.en: And these are the sons of Dishon: Chemdan, and Eshban, and Yitran, and Keran.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי־אֵ֑צֶר בִּלְהָ֥ן וְזַעֲוָ֖ן וַעֲקָֽן׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Etzer: Bilhan, and Za'avan, and Aqan.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֥לֶּה בְנֵֽי־דִישָׁ֖ן ע֥וּץ וַאֲרָֽן׃

i18n.en: These are the sons of Dishan: Utz, and Aran.

paragraphs.text: אֵ֖לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֣י הַחֹרִ֑י אַלּ֤וּף לוֹטָן֙ אַלּ֣וּף שׁוֹבָ֔ל אַלּ֥וּף צִבְע֖וֹן אַלּ֥וּף עֲנָֽה׃

i18n.en: These are the chiefs that came of the Chorim: chief Lotan, chief Shoval, chief Tziv'on, chief Anah,

paragraphs.text: אַלּ֥וּף דִּשֹׁ֛ן אַלּ֥וּף אֵ֖צֶר אַלּ֣וּף דִּישָׁ֑ן אֵ֣לֶּה אַלּוּפֵ֧י הַחֹרִ֛י לְאַלֻּפֵיהֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שֵׂעִֽיר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: chief Dishon, chief Etzer, chief Dishan. These are the chiefs that came of the Chorim, according to their chiefs in the land of Se'ir.

paragraphs.commentary: **The Horite-block closes with a *p'tuchah* (פ) paragraph-marker, confirming the editorial-division between the Horite-block (vv 20-30) and the following king-list (vv 31-39).** The Horite-block is *not* closed with a *hu Edom* refrain (the refrain marks only Esav-blocks), consistent with the editorial-significance of the refrain as a structural-marker of Esavite-units within the chapter.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ הַמְּלָכִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מָלְכ֖וּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם לִפְנֵ֥י מְלָךְ־מֶ֖לֶךְ לִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Yisra'el.

paragraphs.commentary:
**Gen 36:31 is one of the most-decisive documentary-critical anchors in the Pentateuch.** The prefatory formula *lifnei melokh melekh livnei Yisra'el* — *before any king reigned over the children of Yisra'el* — presupposes the Israelite monarchy as already established in the implied-reader's present. The verse's editorial-perspective is therefore post-monarchic at the earliest. The documentary-critical observation is mainstream modern scholarship; it is not a Wheel-of-Heaven distinctive claim.

**The documentary-critical case.** **Wellhausen** *Prolegomena zur Geschichte Israels* 1878 / *Prolegomena to the History of Israel* 1885 (ET) pp. 8-9 is the classic statement: the formula is intelligible only if the reader is already-acquainted with an Israelite monarchy; a Mosaic-period writer could not have written this verse because the Israelite monarchy did not yet exist. The argument is reproduced in **Eissfeldt** *The Old Testament: An Introduction* 1965 (ET) p. 198; **Friedman** *Who Wrote the Bible?* 1987 pp. 33-34 and *The Bible with Sources Revealed* 2003 pp. 96-97 (assigning Gen 36:31-43 to a post-monarchic editorial layer); **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 284; **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 pp. 568-569; **Hamilton** *NICOT* pp. 401-402; **Skinner** *ICC* pp. 434-435; **Sarna** *JPS Genesis* 1989 pp. 252-253.

**The medieval anticipation: Ibn Ezra.** The documentary-critical observation was anticipated by **Ibn Ezra** (1089-1164), whose famously cryptic comment at Gen 36:31 — *v-im tavin sod ha-shneim asar... v-yodaim tidom* (*and if you understand the secret of the twelve... the knowing-ones will keep silent*) — is widely interpreted (Spinoza *Tractatus Theologico-Politicus* 1670 ch. 8; Friedman 1987 pp. 18-22) as Ibn Ezra's coded-acknowledgment that the verse implies post-Mosaic authorship.

**The harmonizing-traditional reading.** **Rashi** at Gen 36:31 reads *lifnei melokh melekh* as referring to the patriarchal-promise of Gen 17:6 / 17:16 / 35:11 (kings will descend from Avraham/Sarah and Ya'aqov); the formula thus refers to the *promised* king rather than to a historically-extant Israelite monarchy. **Cassuto** *The Documentary Hypothesis and the Composition of the Pentateuch* 1941 (ET 1961) is the major modern apologetic statement, treating the formula as predictive or retrospective-narrative-comment.

**The eight-kings-list structure.** Vv 31-39 list eight kings (Bela, Yovav, Chusham, Hadad ben-Bedad, Samlah, Sha'ul, Ba'al-Chanan, Hadar) — **non-dynastic** (each from a different city; no son-of-predecessor formula). **Bartlett** *Edom and the Edomites* JSOTSup 77 (1989) pp. 86-102 reads the list as preserving genuine historical-memory of an Edomite pre-monarchic confederation. The Iron-Age archaeological record at Buseirah (Bozrah, v 33), Tel el-Kheleifeh, Umm el-Biyara, Tawilan supports an Edomite presence in the relevant region from the early Iron Age forward. The Neo-Assyrian record attests Edomite kings from the 9th century BCE; the Gen 36 list represents a pre-Neo-Assyrian phase.

See the central-glossary `edom-kings-before-israel-monarchy-documentary-anchor` entry for the full apparatus.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ בֶּאֱד֔וֹם בֶּ֖לַע בֶּן־בְּע֑וֹר וְשֵׁ֥ם עִיר֖וֹ דִּנְהָֽבָה׃

i18n.en: And Bela the son of Be'or reigned in Edom; and the name of his city was Dinhavah.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The first Edomite king listed is *Bela ben-Be'or* (בֶּלַע בֶּן־בְּעוֹר). The patronymic *ben-Be'or* is shared with *Bil'am ben-Be'or* (בִּלְעָם בֶּן־בְּעוֹר) of Num 22-24, and the personal-names differ by a single mem-suffix from a shared possible Semitic root *b-l-ʿ* (*swallow*).**

**The rabbinic identifying-tradition** (b. Sanhedrin 105a; Targum Pseudo-Jonathan at Gen 36:32; Genesis Rabbah 82:14; Rashi) identifies the Gen 36:32 Bela with the Num 22-24 Bil'am, integrating the Bil'am-prophet-tradition into the Edomite-king-list pre-history.

**The modern critical distinguishing-tradition** (Westermann *Genesis 12-36* p. 567; Hamilton *NICOT* p. 402; Bartlett 1989 pp. 89-90; Speiser p. 283; Levine *Numbers 21-36* AB 2000 pp. 137-156; Sarna p. 253) treats Bela and Bil'am as separate figures sharing a regional onomastic-tradition.

**The Deir 'Alla inscription.** A late-9th / 8th c BCE Aramaic plaster-inscription discovered in 1967 at Tell Deir 'Alla in the Jordan Valley names *Bal'am bar-Be'or* as a *chozeh elahin* (seer of the gods) and preserves a substantial visionary-oracle. The standard editions (Hoftijzer & van der Kooij 1976; Hoftijzer & van der Kooij eds. 1991; Levine *Numbers 21-36* AB 2000 pp. 241-275) confirm the historical-existence of a *Bil'am bar-Be'or* tradition in the Trans-Jordanian region in the early Iron Age, independent of the HB. The inscription supports the modern critical reading that the Bil'am-tradition has a real regional substratum; it does not by itself decide the identification-question with the Gen 36:32 Bela.

See the overlay entry `bela-vs-bilam-ben-beor-name-doublet` for the full apparatus. The chapter-36 anchor is provisional; a future Num 22-Bil'am translation would justify promotion to the central glossary.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֖מָת בָּ֑לַע וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו יוֹבָ֥ב בֶּן־זֶ֖רַח מִבָּצְרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Bela died, and Yovav the son of Zerach of Botzrah reigned in his stead.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֖מָת יוֹבָ֑ב וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו חֻשָׁ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ הַתֵּימָנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Yovav died, and Chusham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֖מָת חֻשָׁ֑ם וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ תַּחְתָּ֜יו הֲדַ֣ד בֶּן־בְּדַ֗ד הַמַּכֶּ֤ה אֶת־מִדְיָן֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב וְשֵׁ֥ם עִיר֖וֹ עֲוִֽית׃

i18n.en: And Chusham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck Midyan in the field of Mo'av, reigned in his stead; and the name of his city was Avit.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The Hadad ben-Bedad notice is editorially-distinctive in the otherwise-formulaic king-list (the standard formula is *va-yamot X va-yimlokh tachtav Y*) by adding a military-historical detail: *ha-makkeh et-Midyan b-sdei Mo'av* (*who struck Midyan in the field of Mo'av*).** The notice is the only non-formulaic content within the eight-kings block and is presumably preserved from a historical-memory source.

**The Edom-Midyan-Mo'av regional triangle is a recurring HB matrix.** **Num 22:4-7** (the Mo'av-Midyan alliance against Israel; Balaq sends elders of both to Bil'am); **Num 25:1-18** (the Ba'al-Pe'or apostasy involving Mo'avite and Midianite women; the Pinchas episode); **Num 31** (the Mosaic war against Midyan); **Judg 6-8** (Gideon's war against Midyan and Amaleq; Judg 8:10-12 — the kings of Midyan Zebach and Tzalmunna). The Keturah-line at Gen 25:1-4 places Midyan and other southern-Arabian tribes within the Abrahamic-collateral genealogy.

The Hadad ben-Bedad notice preserves a fragment of pre-Israelite Trans-Jordanian regional-history: an Edomite king of an earlier era striking the Midianites within Mo'avite territory. Modern critical scholarship (**Bartlett** 1989 pp. 91-92; **Hamilton** *NICOT* p. 403) reads the notice as authentic-historical-memory embedded within the king-list.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֖מָת הֲדָ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו שַׂמְלָ֖ה מִמַּשְׂרֵקָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masreqah reigned in his stead.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֖מָת שַׂמְלָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו שָׁא֖וּל מֵרְחֹב֥וֹת הַנָּהָֽר׃

i18n.en: And Samlah died, and Sha'ul of Rechovot by the river reigned in his stead.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֖מָת שָׁא֑וּל וַיִּמְלֹ֣ךְ תַּחְתָּ֔יו בַּ֥עַל חָנָ֖ן בֶּן־עַכְבּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: And Sha'ul died, and Ba'al-Chanan the son of Akhbor reigned in his stead.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּמָת֮ בַּ֣עַל חָנָ֣ן בֶּן־עַכְבּוֹר֒ וַיִּמְלֹ֤ךְ תַּחְתָּיו֙ הֲדַ֔ר וְשֵׁ֥ם עִיר֖וֹ פָּ֑עוּ וְשֵׁ֨ם אִשְׁתּ֤וֹ מְהֵֽיטַבְאֵל֙ בַּת־מַטְרֵ֔ד בַּ֖ת מֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃

i18n.en: And Ba'al-Chanan the son of Akhbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead; and the name of his city was Pa'u; and his wife's name was Meheitav'el, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mei-Zahav.

paragraphs.commentary:
**The MT reads *Hadar* (הֲדַר); the parallel 1 Chr 1:50 reads *Hadad* (הֲדַד); the Samaritan Pentateuch at Gen 36:39 also reads *Hadad*; the LXX manuscripts vary (*Αδαδ* / *Αδαρ*).** The standard text-critical reading is that the original was *Hadad* (matching the first Hadad of v 35 with a different patronymic; the Edomite-king-onomasticon repeats the Hadad name, consistent with 1 Kgs 11:14-22 where another Hadad the Edomite is a Solomon-period adversary) and that the Gen 36:39 *Hadar* is a scribal-variant arising from the common Hebrew-paleographic resh/dalet confusion (cf. Gen 10:3 *Rifat* / 1 Chr 1:6 *Difat*).

Modern critical editions (BHS apparatus) note the variant. **Speiser** *AB Genesis* 1964 p. 283 and **Westermann** *Genesis 12-36* 1985 p. 567 read either way. ASV / KJV / NJPS translate the MT *Hadar*; some modern translations harmonize to *Hadad*. The translation preserves the MT *Hadar* per the standing principle of translating the principal reading.

**The wife-and-genealogy detail.** *u-shem ishto Meheitav'el bat-Matred bat Mei-Zahav* — *and his wife's name was Meheitav'el, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mei-Zahav*. The notice is the only Edomite-king-wife notice in the list and is matrilineally-extended (the wife's mother *and* maternal-grandmother are named). The Targum and rabbinic tradition reads *Mei-Zahav* (*waters-of-gold*) either as a toponym or as a personal-name; the editorial-significance of preserving the matrilineal-chain across three generations is unresolved.

paragraphs.text: וְ֠אֵלֶּה שְׁמ֞וֹת אַלּוּפֵ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔ם לִמְקֹמֹתָ֖ם בִּשְׁמֹתָ֑ם אַלּ֥וּף תִּמְנָ֛ע אַלּ֥וּף עַֽלְוָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף יְתֵֽת׃

i18n.en: And these are the names of the chiefs that came of Esav, according to their families, after their places, by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Yetet,

paragraphs.commentary: **The second *alufim*-list (vv 40-43) opens with the editorial-superscription *l-mishpechotam li-mqomotam bi-shmotam* — *according to their families, after their places, by their names* — which signals a *toponymic-eponym catalogue*: each *aluf* names both a clan (descended-from-this-eponym) and a geographical territory (named-after-this-eponym).** The names of the second list (Timna, Alvah, Yetet, Oholivamah, Elah, Pinon, Qenaz, Teman, Mivtzar, Magdi'el, Iram) overlap only partially with the first *alufim*-list of vv 15-19 (Teman, Omar, Tzefo, Qenaz, Qorach, Ga'tam, Amaleq, Nachat, Zerach, Shammah, Mizzah, Ye'ush, Ya'lam, Qorach). The non-identity has been read by **Speiser** *AB* pp. 283-284 and **Westermann** pp. 565-567 as evidence that the two lists draw from distinct geographical-source traditions — possibly the v 15-19 list preserves a *bnei Esav* clan-descent register, while the v 40-43 list preserves a *territorial-administrative* register naming the chief-of-each-territory. **Bartlett** 1989 pp. 86-102 reads the second list as preserving the post-monarchic-tribal-confederation phase referenced obliquely at the end of the chapter.

paragraphs.text: אַלּ֧וּף אָהֳלִיבָמָ֛ה אַלּ֥וּף אֵלָ֖ה אַלּ֥וּף פִּינֹֽן׃

i18n.en: chief Oholivamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

paragraphs.text: אַלּ֥וּף קְנַ֛ז אַלּ֥וּף תֵּימָ֖ן אַלּ֥וּף מִבְצָֽר׃

i18n.en: chief Qenaz, chief Teman, chief Mivtzar,

paragraphs.text: אַלּ֥וּף מַגְדִּיאֵ֖ל אַלּ֣וּף עִירָ֑ם אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ אַלּוּפֵ֣י אֱד֗וֹם לְמֹֽשְׁבֹתָם֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ אֲחֻזָּתָ֔ם ה֥וּא עֵשָׂ֖ו אֲבִ֥י אֱדֽוֹם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: chief Magdi'el, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their dwelling-places in the land of their possession. This is Esav, the father of Edom.

paragraphs.commentary: **The chapter closes with the fullest form of the *hu Edom* refrain: *hu Esav avi Edom* — *this is Esav, the father of Edom*.** The closing *p'tuchah* (פ) paragraph-marker confirms the end of the Esav-toledot block. The fourfold-refrain pattern (vv 1, 8, 19, 43, with the v 9 variant *avi Edom*) brackets the chapter's Esavite-units — opening at v 1 (*toledot Esav hu Edom*), closing the introductory section at v 8 (*Esav hu Edom*), closing the first *alufim*-list at v 19 (*hu Edom*), and closing the chapter at v 43 (*hu Esav avi Edom*). The structural-pattern is editorially-deliberate (Skinner, Westermann, Hamilton, Friedman). See the overlay entry `hu-edom-fourfold-refrain-toledot-structure`.
